The SFO Rental Car Center is accessible via the AirTrain Blue Line from all terminals.

Summary
This vegan mushroom risotto serves 4 and achieves a luxurious, creamy texture through the high starch content of arborio rice and the traditional "mantecatura" finishing technique using high-quality olive oil rather than butter. The key is constant agitation to release starch and a vigorous stir at the end to emulsify the fats.

Ingredients
- 1.5 cups Arborio rice (do not rinse)
- 1 lb (450g) Mixed mushrooms (cremini, shiitake, oyster), sliced
- 6 cups Vegetable broth, low sodium (keep simmering in a separate pot)
- 1 small Yellow onion, finely diced
- 2 cloves Garlic, minced
- 1/2 cup Dry white wine (Sauvignon Blanc or Pinot Grigio) or extra broth
- 4 tbsp Extra virgin olive oil, divided
- 2 tbsp Nutritional yeast (optional, adds savory "cheesy" depth)
- 1 tsp Fresh thyme leaves
- Salt and black pepper to taste
- Fresh parsley, chopped (for garnish)

Instructions
1. **Sear the Mushrooms:**
   Heat 1 tbsp olive oil in a large, heavy-bottomed pot over medium-high heat. Add mushrooms and cook until browned and liquid has evaporated (about 5-8 minutes). Remove mushrooms from the pot and set aside.

2. **Toast the Rice:**
   Reduce heat to medium. Add 1 tbsp olive oil and the diced onion to the pot. Sauté until translucent (3-4 minutes). Add the arborio rice and toast, stirring constantly, for 1-2 minutes until the edges of the grains are translucent. Add garlic and thyme, cooking for another 30 seconds until fragrant.

3. **Deglaze:**
   Pour in the white wine. Stir constantly until the wine is fully absorbed by the rice.

4. **The Risotto Method:**
   Add the hot vegetable broth one ladle (approx. 1/2 cup) at a time. Stir frequently. Wait until the liquid is almost completely absorbed before adding the next ladle. This process should take 18-20 minutes. The constant stirring is crucial for releasing starch.

5. **Finish (The Creamy Step):**
   Taste the rice; it should be tender but with a slight bite (al dente). If it is too hard, add a splash more broth.
   **Crucial Step:** Remove the pot from the heat. Stir in the cooked mushrooms, nutritional yeast, and the remaining 2 tbsp of olive oil. Stir vigorously for 30 seconds to emulsify the oil with the starchy liquid—this creates the creamy texture without dairy.

6. **Serve:**
   Season with salt and plenty of black pepper. Garnish with fresh parsley and serve immediately.

Secrets to Dairy-Free Creaminess
| Technique | Why it works |
| :--- | :--- |
| **Do Not Rinse** | Retains the surface starch on the arborio rice, which is essential for thickening the broth. |
| **Hot Broth Only** | Adding cold broth shocks the rice and stops the cooking process; keeping broth hot ensures consistent starch release. |
| **Agitation** | Stirring causes rice grains to rub against each other, releasing amylopectin (starch) into the liquid. |
| **Mantecatura** | The final vigorous stir off the heat with fat (olive oil) creates a stable emulsion, mimicking the texture of butter and cheese. |

Summary
This wedding day timeline is designed for a 4:00 PM ceremony on Saturday, June 15, 2025. The schedule incorporates your requested milestones—First Look, Photos, Cocktail Hour, Grand Entrance, Dinner, Speeches, and First Dance—while ensuring adequate buffer time for guest movement and transitions between event spaces.

Assumptions
- The ceremony and reception take place at the same venue or within a 15-minute drive.
- The ceremony length is approximately 30 minutes.
- Dinner service is plated or buffet style requiring about 60 minutes.
- The reception concludes around 10:00 PM or 11:00 PM.

Structured Details
Time | Activity | Notes & Buffer
2:00 PM | First Look | Intimate session; includes 30-min buffer before group photos
2:30 PM | Wedding Party Photos | 60-min block; wrap up by 3:30 PM for pre-ceremony refresh
4:00 PM | Ceremony Starts | 30-45 mins; guests seated by 3:55 PM
4:45 PM | Cocktail Hour | 60 mins; couple takes sunset photos or joins guests
6:00 PM | Grand Entrance | 15-min transition buffer for guests to find seats
6:15 PM | Dinner Service | 60 mins; includes time for plating and eating
7:15 PM | Speeches & Toasts | 30 mins; scheduled as dinner concludes
7:45 PM | First Dance | Opens the dance floor immediately after

Logistics and Transition Buffers
Pre-Ceremony Buffer (3:30 PM - 4:00 PM):
The photo session ends 30 minutes before the ceremony. This "hideaway" time allows the wedding party to freshen up, drink water, and relax while guests arrive and take their seats.

Cocktail to Reception Transition (5:45 PM - 6:00 PM):
Cocktail hour is listed as starting at 4:45 PM. Guests should begin moving to the dining area around 5:45 PM. The Grand Entrance is scheduled for 6:00 PM to ensure the room is full and seated before the couple is announced.

Dinner Flow:
Speeches are scheduled for 7:15 PM, towards the end of the meal service. This prevents interruptions while guests are receiving hot food and ensures the staff has cleared plates before the formal toasts begin.

Summary
This 3-day itinerary for April 5-7, 2024, focuses on Kyoto's most iconic historical sites while keeping children engaged with nature and animals. The schedule is optimized for public transit access to minimize walking between stops, ensuring no leg requires more than a 15-20 minute walk. As this falls during the late cherry blossom (sakura) season, expect crowds and start days early (around 8:30 AM).

Assumptions
Travel relies on trains and buses (ICOCA/Suica cards recommended). The family is staying near a central hub like Kyoto Station or Kawaramachi.

Structured Details

Option 1: Day 1 - The Red Gates & Old Kyoto | Fushimi Inari & Kiyomizu-dera | Activity Level: Moderate (Steps)
Start at Fushimi Inari Taisha (JR Inari Station, 0 min walk). The "Senbon Torii" gate tunnel is visually stunning for kids; hike to the Yotsutsuji intersection for views and turn back to save energy. Afternoon: Take a taxi (approx. 1500 JPY) or bus to Kiyomizu-dera to avoid the steep uphill approach. Explore the temple and the historic Ninenzaka streets.
Dinner: Conveyor belt sushi (Kaiten-zushi) near Kyoto Station (e.g., Sushiro or Kura Sushi).
Action: [Button: Fushimi Inari Guide] https://www.japan-guide.com/e/e3915.html

Option 2: Day 2 - Arashiyama Nature & Monkeys | Bamboo Grove & Monkey Park | Activity Level: Active (Easy Hike)
Take the JR Sagano Line to Saga-Arashiyama Station. Walk to the Bamboo Grove (10 mins). Visit Tenryu-ji Temple (adjacent). Cross the Togetsukyo Bridge to the Iwatayama Monkey Park (entrance is close to the bridge). The hike up is about 20 minutes but manageable for ages 8-10, rewarding them with wild monkeys they can feed safely.
Lunch: Udon or Soba noodles in Arashiyama; many shops offer kid-friendly sets.
Action: [Button: Arashiyama Guide] https://www.japan-guide.com/e/e3912.html

Option 3: Day 3 - Gold & Shoguns | Kinkaku-ji & Nijo Castle | Activity Level: Light
Morning: Kinkaku-ji (Golden Pavilion). Accessible via Kyoto City Bus (approx. 40 mins from station). The loop around the pond is flat and short. Afternoon: Nijo Castle (Nightingale floors squeak when walked on, fascinating for kids). The castle grounds have wide paths and gardens.
Dinner: Okonomiyaki (Japanese savory pancake) where staff cook it in front of you.
Action: [Button: Kinkaku-ji Guide] https://www.japan-guide.com/e/e3908.html

Summary
January is widely considered the peak season for Bangkok and the winter season for Hanoi. The climates are distinctly different: Bangkok is tropical, dry, and warm (often hot by midday), while Hanoi is subtropical, cool, and frequently overcast with mist. For a walking tour, Hanoi offers much more comfortable temperatures for physical exertion, but Bangkok offers brighter skies and sunshine.

Structured Details
Metric | Bangkok, Thailand | Hanoi, Vietnam | Walking Tour Verdict
Average High Temp | 32 C (90 F) | 20 C (68 F) | Hanoi is significantly cooler and sweat-free.
Average Low Temp | 22 C (72 F) | 14 C (57 F) | Bangkok has pleasant evenings; Hanoi requires a light jacket.
Humidity | Moderate (60-70%) | High (75-85%) | Bangkok feels drier; Hanoi feels damp and chilly.
Rainfall Probability | Very Low (< 2 days) | Low (Drizzle/Mist common) | Bangkok is reliably dry; Hanoi has persistent mist but rarely heavy rain.
Sky Conditions | Mostly Sunny | Often Overcast/Gray | Bangkok is better for bright photography.

Check Live Hanoi Weather: https://weather.com/weather/today/l/VMXX0006:1:VM
